title: Ah, pietà! Signori miei!
subtitle: Leporello: aria from Don Giovanni, Act 2 (No. 20)

passages.label: Ah, pietà! Signori miei! … Dò ragione a voi, a lei
Ma, ma, il delitto mio non è · Il padron con prepotenza l'innocenza mi rubò
Donna Elvira! compatite! · Voi capite come andò
Di Masetto non sò nulla … che con lei girando vo
Ah voi, Signore! · certo timore, certo accidente … poi qui celato
l'affar si sa · ma s'io sapeva, fuggia per quà! (to the end)

licences.source: W. A. Mozart, Don Giovanni, K. 527 (1787), Act 2 scene 9, No. 20 Aria
licences.author: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791)

licences.source: Lorenzo Da Ponte, libretto of Don Giovanni (1787)
licences.author: Lorenzo Da Ponte (1749–1838)
licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score (Dò, sò and quà with their accents, Ah voi, Signore!, È un oretta, dentro oscuro, là porta, io me-ne vo hyphenated as one word, fuggia on two notes, and the full stop after per in bar 97; the libretto has Do, so, qua, A voi, signore, un'oretta, dentro scuro, la porta, me ne vo and fuggìa).

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 213–217, bars 1–106 of No. 20
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the sung line and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, then checked bar by bar and checked again by a fresh checker (clean). The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out; Donna Elvira, Zerlina, Don Ottavio and Masetto are on stage but do not sing. The piano's 8va passage in bars 6–7 is written at sounding pitch; stray printed dots in bars 26 and 86 are not read as dotted rhythms. In bar 55 the first C of the voice has only an English syllable under it and is kept as printed, with no Italian word. Playback tempo: Allegro assai ♩ = 242 (a half note = 121), about 1:45, from the median (1:45) of five complete recordings whose track holds the aria alone (Giulini 1959 1:52, Böhm 1967 1:45, Fricsay 1958 1:45, Haitink 1984 1:42, Jacobs 2006 1:42). Mozart gives the words only.
